title: Creator: smooth face, painted eyes, straight legs, anime hair and clothes
question: Are the face, eyes, legs, hair and clothes good enough now to build new characters on?

options.label: base-ok
options.note: Good enough to build characters on. Face: Eric's base is smooth shaded like his model. Eyes: all styles come from the painted anime eyes. Legs: straightened and evened out. Hair: seven styles built from pointed, faceted locks like the originals (messy short, spiky, long straight, bob, twin tails, high ponytail, buns), fringes stop above the eyes, an optional second colour on inner locks and tips, and Mio's ears fold in under made hair. Clothes: hoodie (hood, drawstrings, pocket, ribbed cuffs), sailor blouse (collar with stripe, bow), shirt with collar and tie, blazer (lapels, buttons, pocket flaps, shirt and tie in the V), ringer tee; slim trousers (belt, buckle, crease and knee folds, back pockets), cargo shorts (side pockets, turned-up cuffs), pleated skirt with stripes; sneakers, loafers, boots. Also fixed: cuffs and hems are closed, the skirt sides stay clear of the hanging hands, shirt necklines keep Eric's shoulders covered, and Eric's stubble is its own choice (his sideburns still go with his own hair).

options.label: needs-work
options.note: Tell me what to fix first. What I can still see: the made hair is less chunky than the originals' big clumps, and the locks read a bit striped up close; Mio's and Eric's hands are still the originals' blocky hands; at the far end of a walking stride the forward thigh grazes the pleated skirt's hem (a long skirt and a knee-length A-line were tried and dropped, they tore in the walk); the face skin on the bare base is lighter and plainer than the original's, because the hair paint was cleaned off the texture in the last round; the buns are small.

decision: Jørgen in chat, 2026-09-30: characters still look bow-legged. Hair looks kind of creepy rather than the cute artisan feel of Emi[Mio] and Eric's originals. Rest of the body a little better. Eyes much better. Clothes need more work to look as well crafted as the existing ones; give them volume.
